question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=2 x^{2} + x - 2$ at the point $(1,1)$ intersects the $y$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate the polynomial.

$$
f'(x)=4 x + 1.
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(1)&=4 (1) + 1=5, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(5)}=- \frac{1}{5}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(1,1)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(1)&=- \frac{1}{5}(x-(1)), \\y&=- \frac{x}{5} + \frac{6}{5}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=- \frac{1}{5}\cdot 0+\left(\frac{6}{5}\right), \\y&=\frac{6}{5}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(0,\frac{6}{5})$.
